surfaces.part: iron post with gold bands and star finial

answer.evidence: The square pedestal (width 14, rows 36-45) shows a light top face in rows 36-41. A darker front-edge row and shadow at about rows 41-42 separate it from a 4-row front face in rows 42-45 with a small emblem. Each lantern has a sloped blue crown roof in rows 13-17 that widens to a gold eave line at rows 18-19, and the lit glass body hangs below it. The thin post is a vertical structure carried by the pedestal. The pedestal top is clearly more than a 1-2 row rim, so the object reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, sparse prop, so I judged it by eye against prop-lamp-crook and the well and stall. It has 14 visible tones on its full tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 25 total colours. The reference lamp-crook has only 14 colours in total and no full-tile tone count. The candidate carries clearly more structure: a stone pedestal with a visible top face, an iron post with gold bands, a star finial, a curled crossarm and two crowned lanterns with warm lit glass. Each material gets roughly 3-5 tones, a bit below the 5-6 of the richer references such as the well and stall. 62% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral. That is the iron-post look, and the reference lamp (100% neutral) is the same. The glass, gold and stone parts are separated by value, not by a uniform black sticker outline, so I call the outline mixed. It has no large flat fills. A careful artist would accept it next to the reference lamp without it looking thinner or flatter.
